places.name: Ceuta
places.significance: Spanish enclave on the African shore of the Strait of Gibraltar — with Melilla, one of Spain's two cities on mainland Africa
notes: A small landmass in Africa administered by another country — Spain

places.name: Gibraltar
places.significance: British Overseas Territory on Spain's southern tip — the Rock that guards the Atlantic entrance to the Mediterranean
notes: A small landmass administered by another country — the United Kingdom

places.name: Sinai Peninsula
places.significance: Egypt's land bridge to Asia, between the Gulfs of Suez and Aqaba — the only part of Egypt that lies in Asia
notes: The Suez Canal runs along its western edge

places.name: Rabat
places.significance: Capital of Morocco on the Atlantic — the royal and administrative seat, while Casablanca is the business capital

places.name: Casablanca
places.significance: Morocco's largest city, chief port and business capital — a centre of the chemical industry

places.name: Marrakech
places.significance: The Red City, named for its red walls, below the High Atlas — one of Morocco's historic imperial cities

places.name: Tangier
places.significance: Port at the Atlantic mouth of the Strait of Gibraltar — its Tanger Med port is among Africa's largest container ports

places.name: Algiers
places.significance: Capital of Algeria, Africa's largest country, on the Mediterranean — its old Casbah is a World Heritage Site

places.name: Tunis
places.significance: Capital of Africa's northernmost country, on a Mediterranean lagoon beside the ruins of Carthage

places.name: Tripoli
places.significance: Capital of Libya, on the Mediterranean in the west — the country holds Africa's largest proven oil reserves

places.name: Benghazi
places.significance: Libya's second city and eastern port, on the Gulf of Sidra — the hub of the oil-rich east

places.name: Cairo
places.significance: Capital of Egypt at the head of the Nile delta — the largest city in the Arab world, beside the Pyramids of Giza
notes: Egypt: north → Mediterranean Sea, east → Red Sea

places.name: Port Said
places.significance: Port at the Mediterranean mouth of the Suez Canal — a transhipment hub for the canal's traffic

places.name: Alexandria
places.significance: Egypt's chief port and second city, founded by Alexander the Great on the western edge of the Nile delta — once home of the great Library and the Pharos lighthouse
notes: Near the mouth of the Nile

places.name: Suez
places.significance: City at the Red Sea end of Egypt's great canal — its southern gateway, with Port Said at the northern end

places.name: Horn of Africa
places.significance: The continent's eastern tip, jutting into the Arabian Sea between the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean

places.name: Khartoum
places.significance: Capital of Sudan, where the Blue and White Nile meet

places.name: Juba
places.significance: Capital of South Sudan, the world's newest country (independent in 2011), on the White Nile

places.name: Mogadishu
places.significance: Capital of Somalia and its chief port, on the Indian Ocean

places.name: Berbera
places.significance: Deep-water port on the Gulf of Aden, in self-declared Somaliland — a strategic harbour near the Bab-el-Mandeb

places.name: Asmara
places.significance: Capital of Eritrea, high on its plateau at over 2,300m — a World Heritage modernist city of Italian colonial architecture

places.name: Massawa
places.significance: Eritrea's main Red Sea port, among the hottest towns on earth

places.name: Addis Ababa
places.significance: Capital of Ethiopia, high on the Ethiopian Highlands — headquarters of the African Union

places.name: Danakil Depression
places.significance: One of the hottest and lowest places on earth, over 100m below sea level — salt flats, and the lava lake of Erta Ale

places.name: Afar Region
places.significance: Ethiopia's hot, low north-east, where three tectonic plates pull apart — and where the fossil 'Lucy' was found

places.name: Djibouti City
places.significance: Capital and port of the small state guarding the Bab-el-Mandeb — host to US, French and Chinese military bases, and Ethiopia's main outlet to the sea

places.name: Nairobi
places.significance: Capital of Kenya and East Africa's business hub — headquarters of the UN Environment Programme

places.name: Mombasa
places.significance: Kenya's chief port and East Africa's busiest — the sea gateway for landlocked Uganda, Rwanda and South Sudan

places.name: Kampala
places.significance: Capital of Uganda, built on hills beside Lake Victoria, the source of the White Nile

places.name: Kigali
places.significance: Capital of Rwanda, the 'land of a thousand hills' — known as one of Africa's cleanest cities

places.name: Gitega
places.significance: Capital of Burundi since 2019, replacing Bujumbura on Lake Tanganyika

places.name: Dodoma
places.significance: Official capital of Tanzania, chosen in 1973 for its central position — Dar es Salaam remains the commercial capital

places.name: Dar es Salaam
places.significance: Tanzania's largest city, chief port and former capital — the TAZARA railway links it to Zambia

places.name: Zanzibar
places.significance: The Spice Island of the Indian Ocean — cloves, and Stone Town, the old Swahili trading port

places.name: Pemba
places.significance: The northern isle of the Spice Islands, and the chief grower of their cloves

places.name: Ilhéu das Rolas
places.significance: Islet off São Tomé where the Equator crosses land in the Gulf of Guinea — a monument marks the line
notes: Too small for the map's outline of São Tomé and Príncipe: the main island ends about 3km north of the Equator

places.name: Lilongwe
places.significance: Capital of Malawi since 1975, replacing Zomba — in the central highlands of a long, lake-bound country

places.name: Maputo
places.significance: Capital and chief port of Mozambique, on Delagoa Bay in the far south — a sea outlet for South Africa and Eswatini

places.name: Lusaka
places.significance: Capital of landlocked Zambia, whose copper reaches the sea by the TAZARA railway to Dar es Salaam

places.name: Harare
places.significance: Capital of Zimbabwe on the Highveld, known as Salisbury until 1982

places.name: Gaborone
places.significance: Capital of Botswana, among the world's largest diamond producers by value, near the South African border

places.name: Pretoria
places.significance: South Africa's executive capital, the seat of government at the Union Buildings — the Jacaranda City
notes: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria (executive), Cape Town (legislative), Bloemfontein (judicial)
Two countries lie within South Africa's borders: Eswatini and Lesotho

places.name: Cape Town
places.significance: South Africa's legislative capital, where Parliament sits, beneath Table Mountain

places.name: Bloemfontein
places.significance: South Africa's judicial capital, seat of the Supreme Court of Appeal, in the Free State

places.name: Kimberley
places.significance: Diamond city of the 1870s rush — the Big Hole, one of the largest hand-dug excavations on earth

places.name: Johannesburg
places.significance: City of gold, born of the 1886 Witwatersrand gold rush — South Africa's largest city and economic hub

places.name: Durban
places.significance: South Africa's busiest port, the busiest in sub-Saharan Africa, on the Indian Ocean

places.name: East London
places.significance: South Africa's only river port, at the mouth of the Buffalo River on the Indian Ocean

places.name: Cape of Good Hope
places.significance: Rocky headland at the tip of the Cape Peninsula — first rounded by Bartolomeu Dias in 1488, the turning point of the sea route to India

places.name: Luanda
places.significance: Capital and chief port of Angola, on the Atlantic — one of Africa's leading oil exporters

places.name: Windhoek
places.significance: Capital of Namibia, on the central plateau between the Namib and Kalahari deserts

places.name: Kinshasa
places.significance: Capital of DR Congo on the Congo River, facing Brazzaville — Africa's largest French-speaking city

places.name: Brazzaville
places.significance: Capital of the Republic of the Congo, facing Kinshasa across the Congo River — the closest pair of capitals bar Rome and the Vatican

places.name: Bamako
places.significance: Capital of landlocked Mali, on the Niger River — heartland of the medieval Mali Empire of Timbuktu

places.name: Niamey
places.significance: Capital of Niger, on the Niger River — Niger is one of the world's major uranium producers
notes: Niger is landlocked, north of Nigeria

places.name: Abuja
places.significance: Capital of Nigeria, Africa's most populous country — a planned city that replaced Lagos in 1991

places.name: Accra
places.significance: Capital of Ghana, the first sub-Saharan colony to win independence (1957) — and Ghana a leading cocoa grower

places.name: Grain Coast
places.significance: Liberia's shore of the Gulf of Guinea, named for a spice the Portuguese once traded there

places.name: Ivory Coast
places.significance: The shore between Liberia and Ghana, named for the elephant tusks once traded there

places.name: Gold Coast
places.significance: Ghana's shore, named for the precious metal traded there — and the country's own name under British rule

places.name: Slave Coast
places.significance: The shore of Togo and Benin on the Bight of Benin, named for the Atlantic trade in captive Africans

groups.name: North Africa
groups.mnemonic: MATLE ("Tension mat le") — Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt, west to east along the Mediterranean

groups.name: Libya on the map
groups.mnemonic: Find the L in the map — Libya

groups.name: Kenya to Mozambique
groups.mnemonic: K → T → M₁, M₂ — Kenya, then Tanzania, then Malawi and Mozambique, north to south

groups.name: Zambia and Zimbabwe
groups.mnemonic: Z₁ → Z₂ — Zambia, then Zimbabwe below it

groups.name: Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi
groups.mnemonic: U ← R ← B, उल्टी coffee — Burundi, Rwanda, Uganda going north: Gitega, Kigali, Kampala

groups.name: Lilongwe
groups.mnemonic: Gale ki MALA LAMBI (long) hai — MALAwi, LiLONGwe

groups.name: Harare
groups.mnemonic: HAR jaate hai hmesha — HARare, Zimbabwe

groups.name: Angola
groups.mnemonic: 'A' इसलिए ऊपर — the A of BAN sits on top: Angola is above Namibia and Botswana

groups.name: Group of C
groups.mnemonic: Group of C — C₁ DRC (Bada Congo), C₂ Chhota Congo, C₃ CAR, C₄ Chad, C₅ Cameroon

groups.name: Nigeria and Niger
groups.mnemonic: N₁ → Nigeria (Ria → coastline); N₂ → Niger (landlocked, north of Nigeria)

groups.name: West Africa's coast
groups.mnemonic: MS GS LCD GTB — Mauritania, Senegal · Guinea, Sierra Leone · Liberia, Côte d'Ivoire · Ghana, Togo, Benin

groups.name: 2 G's near Senegal
groups.mnemonic: 2 G's near Senegal — Gambia and Guinea-Bissau
